intro: Lesson 28: Choosing the type of enquiry. To understand that different questions need different types of scientific enquiry

questions.q: 'Are seeds from bigger fruits bigger?' Which type of enquiry?
questions.model: Can we change a fruit's size? No. So collect lots of fruits, measure fruit and seed sizes, and look for a link: pattern seeking.

questions.q: 'How can we sort these shells?' Which type?
Match eight questions on the sheet to their type of enquiry and give a reason for each.
questions.a: Correct matches with reasons (as on the answer sheet)
questions.model: Teacher does the first: 'How does ice melt over an hour? Observation over time, because we watch it change.'

questions.q: Write your own question for each type of enquiry.
Pick one pattern-seeking question and plan what data you would collect.
questions.a: e.g. measure height and foot length of 10 family members

questions.q: Watching a bean grow over weeks is...
Big question: why can you not fair-test height and foot size?
questions.a: We cannot change someone's height; we collect data and look for a pattern.
